_doc: Per-corner overrides for tools/place_signs.py / tools/author_signs_blend.py (W1-6 Large Arrow signs AT tight corners, Kevin 2026-10-10: 'they go AT the corner, just past the outside edge'). The rule detects corners itself; an entry here NAMES a detected corner (matched by ribbon + vertex within 30 m of the detected apex — stale after a centreline regen = refused with a WARN) and may skip it, force it, slide it along the curb, pin its base, or re-aim it. Ids: M<k> mainline in station order from the lap seam, connector corners <DC0|DC1|DCL|MED>-<k> (survey numbering); each connector corner yields a -fwd and a -rev sign because side streets are two-way. 'ship' is a note for Kevin, not read by the tools: the six mainline plates are the first seat test; set defaults.include_connectors=false to ship only those.

defaults._doc: see place_signs.DEFAULTS; lateral offsets = curb face 0.08 + raised walk 1.8 (1.5 connector) - 0.25 back-of-walk set-back; height 2.13 m = MUTCD 2A.15 7 ft over a sidewalk; om1_3 = the Type N-1(CA) all-yellow diamond under every arrow (CA MUTCD 2C.10 'should')

M1.where: 70th St / Alvarado Rd - the lap-seam right-hander onto Alvarado
M1.note: R 12 m, ~95 deg; the ribbon width steps 27.5 -> 17 m across the seam so the Blender ROAD ray-cast is authoritative here; slide_along_curb_m / base_xz are the backstop

M2.note: R 9 m, ~180 deg hairpin: two W1-6R (first where hard turning starts at the R 60 crossing, second from the R 20 crossing at the tip, ~50 m on). Four W1-8R chevrons are the opt-in replacement for the second arrow if it reads wrong from the seat

M3.note: R 10 m, ~110 deg; 4-lane approach so lane_off is ~5 m right of the centreline - if the plate looks one lane off from the seat, slide_along_curb_m, not the formula

M4.note: R 10 m, ~110 deg; Navajo's median run ends 22 verts before the apex, no island term

M5.note: R 11 m, ~90 deg; palm ~4-5 m away passes clearance but may sit in the sight line

MED-1.where: Wisconsin Ave / Connecticut Ave - residential right-angle 28 m in from the Lake Murray Blvd mouth
MED-1.note: the -rev plate stands in the Wisconsin throat ~19 m from the mouth cut with the MED-2 jog behind it - the fiddliest spot on the track, check its diagram first; skip:true drops both

MED-6.where: Connecticut Ave -> Delaware Ave, the sharpest connector corner (R 5.7 m, 120 deg)

MED-7.where: Delaware Ave -> Pennsylvania Ln (R 14 m, 48 deg - kept by the 45-deg floor)
MED-7.note: the -rev ray exits ~1 m past the PT and qualifies via the +10 m in-arc tolerance; drop the rev plate with skip if it reads odd

MED-8.where: Pennsylvania Ln -> Colorado Ave right-angle after the connector's longest straight (189 m)

MED-10.where: Colorado Ave -> Adelante Ave (R 11 m, 63 deg)

MED-13.where: Airoso Ave -> Del Cerro Ave (R 13.5 m, 98 deg)

DCL-2.where: Del Cerro Blvd loop, the far (east) turnaround (R 4.6 m, 150 deg)
DCL-2.note: probably a cul-de-sac loop turnaround nobody signs in reality - Kevin's call; skip:true drops both approaches

MED-16.reason: the stem arriving at the Del Cerro Blvd / Madra Ave T: a W1-7 Two-Direction Large Arrow on Del Cerro's far (north) curb is the second-pass device, not a W1-6 on the stem

DCL-1.reason: junction with the del_cerro_blvd#1 trunk: the forward ray runs down the trunk and never leaves pavement; a W1-7 across the loop for traffic arriving on the trunk is a second-pass candidate
DCL-1.where: Del Cerro Blvd / Regis Ave turnaround
